title: (III) ESCHATOLOGY: On knowledge as the prerequisite for salvation
english_translation:
[R] {ad.1} ... for it is all mixed with evil, limited in time and space, and transient.

{ad.2} And the wise and those of select judgement are able to recognize the limit- less, timeless, and unmixed (5) goodness of Paradise by the limitedness in time and space and mixture of the goodness in the material world.

{ad.3} And likewise the existence of the countless (10) and limitless evil of Hell can be known from the countable and limited evil that is seen in the material world.

{ad.4} And if, in the material world, the limited and transient goodness and evil, as well as their mixture with each other, could not be seen, then (15) the notion of getting away from evil and of coming to goodness could not occur to the thought of anybody.

{ad.5} And if the soul did not see the knowledge that has accrued to it through 10,000 births, ...

[V] {ad.6} [ ... it would not be able?] to recognize the profit that comes from the eternal, timeless, and unmixed goodness.
Then he needs a leader and guide who can show him the road and passsage to be delivered (5) from the evil and to come to the eternal, unmixed, and intransient Soul.

{ad.7} But, just in case anybody may say that if knowledge can only come to mankind through the Doors which I (10)

have written above, then each person should have these Doors soundly in knowledge, and equally and in like manner, then the answer about this matter is the following:

{ad.8} In many places in this book (15) I have shown the reason for sectarianism is greater or lesser knowledge of the mix- ture. And he who thinks this or says (it), in that (20) [ ... ] he [ ... ] Now that I have ... this [ ... ] mankind [ ... ]
